findings.description: The new under-lock recheck reads only the session's state. `pup retire` never changes state; it appends a `retired` event and leaves the session `merged`. So a `pup fix` that waited behind a `pup retire` passes every check and brings the retired branch back, which the ADR and the docblock say this change prevents.
findings.body:
The new guard at [fix-round.service.ts#L946-L952](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L946-L952) refuses only when `state !== 'merged'`. `pup retire` never moves the state. Under the lock it runs `assertStillMerged`, then `tearDown` (which removes the worktree and deletes the branch), then `appendEvent(db, session.id, 'retired', ...)`, and does nothing else ([session-retire.service.ts#L101-L118](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/session-retire.service.ts#L101-L118)). The rest of `assertStillPinned` passes as well:
- `newestMerge` stops only at `landed` or `merge`. It skips `retired` and still returns the pinned merge.
- The PR was closed without merging, so the pin is not an ancestor of `origin/<target>`.

**Trigger:**
1. `pup fix s1` reads the PR while it is OPEN, then waits behind a gate that holds the lock.
2. The operator closes the PR and runs `pup retire s1 --superseded-by N`, which also waits.
3. `withMergeLock` polls with no fairness, so retire can take the lock first.
4. The fix takes the lock after it.

**Result:**
- `restoreWorktree` finds no branch and runs `worktree add -b pup/s1 ... <pin>`, which recreates the retired branch and worktree.
- `takeFixRoundEdge` moves the retired session from merged to running.
- A worker is started against a CLOSED PR.

Before this PR the wait was `0`, so a fix could never wait behind a retire. The wait added here is what opens the race. The docblock (L928-932) and the ADR 88 amendment both name this exact case as one the recheck prevents. The new test only simulates a holder that sets `state = 'running'`.

**Fix:** also refuse when the newest of the session's `merge`, `landed` and `retired` events is `retired`, as `newestStanding` in `session-retire.service.ts` does. Add a test where the holder appends a `retired` event.

findings.description: `startFixRound` now always waits up to `MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` (125 min). Its second caller, the web dashboard's `fix` action, is documented to refuse at once, so a page click on a held lock now hangs the request. It also stalls the dashboard's Ctrl-C shutdown for up to two hours.
findings.body:
The ADR amendment says "with no flag: like `pup retire`, its only caller is the CLI" ([0088#L248-L249](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/docs/adr/0088-the-merge-lock-records-its-holder-survives-every.md#L248-L249)). That is not true: `runAction`'s `fix` case calls `startFixRound` directly ([web-dashboard-actions.service.ts#L170-L178](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/web-dashboard-actions.service.ts#L170-L178)).

That file's own contract ([L111-L112](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/web-dashboard-actions.service.ts#L111-L112)) says: "The merge gate, the land and the fix round take no lock wait: a page refuses at once where the CLI waits." Merge and land keep that contract through `req.wait`, which only the CLI sets ([merge-gate.service.ts#L1389](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1389), [land.service.ts#L310](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/land.service.ts#L310)). This PR hard-codes the wait for fix instead ([fix-round.service.ts#L271](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L271)).

**Trigger:** the operator clicks Fix on the page while any gate holds the lock.

**Result:**
- The request hangs for up to the full wait instead of refusing at once.
- The "Waiting for the merge lock" line goes to the server's stderr, not to the page.
- The round may start long after the page gave up.
- The first Ctrl-C on `pup dashboard` runs `close()`, which awaits `desk.settle()` ([web-dashboard.service.ts#L227-L233](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/25133c3acf5b39f9f6e80b6c3dbffa50f7b05d1b/src/core/web-dashboard.service.ts#L227-L233)). Shutdown therefore stalls until the wait ends; only a second Ctrl-C kills the process.

`web-dashboard-actions.test.ts` mocks `startFixRound`, so the suite cannot catch this.

**Fix:** give `FixRoundRequest` a `wait?: boolean` as `MergeRequest` and `LandRequest` have, pass `req.wait ? MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS : 0`, set `wait: true` only in the CLI's `pup fix` action, and correct the ADR sentence.

findings.description: The comment's new clause "waiting for a live holder as they do (decision 88)" repeats what the `MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` argument and `withMergeLock`'s JSDoc already say; the original two-line comment was enough.

If a `pup plan edit --rescope` lands while `pup fix` waits for the lock, `takeFixRoundEdge` refuses only after `restoreWorktree` has already added the worktree and branch, and nothing removes them. The refusal says no round was started, yet the next `pup fix` refuses on the leftover worktree. The new 125-minute wait widens a window that used to be seconds.
